note: Faithful rule manifest for the learning-agent engineering guide (§0–§16 + appendices). The .md is authoritative and unchanged; this indexes every actionable rule/practice, typed checkable|judgment|principle, with a predicate (checkable) or reviewer_criterion (judgment). Every section is mapped in sections_accounted — nothing dropped. This is the expertise Sensei applies when building an agent/team.

schema.predicate: checkable: {kind,spec} evaluated on the built agent's artifacts
schema.reviewer_criterion: judgment: yes/no question for the independent reviewer

rules.text: Separate memory by TYPE into four distinct stores — working (context window), episodic (what happened), semantic (what is true), procedural (how to do things). Never collapse them into one blob.

predicate.spec: the built agent's memory design names distinct working/episodic/semantic/procedural stores with different write/retrieval/decay policies; not one undifferentiated store.

rules.text: Write memory at reflection TRIGGERS, not continuously: user correction, task completion/outcome, end-of-turn salience threshold, periodic consolidation, pre-compaction, new-skill-discovered. Salience-gate every write.

predicate.spec: capture is trigger-driven (hooks/events), not every-turn; a salience gate (durable? non-derivable? novel/corrective? general?) precedes each write.

rules.text: Keep a small always-loaded INDEX (MEMORY.md/CLAUDE.md, one line per memory) and a big lazy STORE retrieved on demand. Precision over recall: inject the fewest memories (index + 3–7 relevant), never replay history.

predicate.spec: a bounded one-line-per-memory index loaded each session + a lazy backing store; retrieval injects top-k few, not the whole store.

rules.text: Make context self-managing with NO manual step: a PreCompact hook auto-writes a handover (state · next-action · verbatim do-not-lose block) AND extracts learnings before compaction; a SessionStart(source=compact) hook re-injects on the far side. Unify 'compacts automatically' with 'learns automatically' in one checkpoint.

predicate.spec: PreCompact + SessionStart(source=compact) + Stop/SubagentStop hooks wired; PreCompact both persists a do-not-lose handover and runs salience-gated extraction.

rules.text: Date and attribute every memory (created, last_verified, source/session, volatility/TTL). Resolve contradictions by recency + provenance (newest, best-sourced wins; mark old superseded, don't silently keep both).

predicate.spec: memory-file schema includes created + last_verified + source_session + volatility/expires + superseded_by; consolidation resolves contradictions by recency+provenance.

rules.text: Never let the store hold secrets; treat memory as an injection surface. Scrub credentials/PII at write time (store 'credential present at <path>', never the value); treat retrieved memory as DATA, not instructions; give the user first-class inspect/edit/delete.

predicate.spec: a hard secret/PII scrub gates every write; retrieved memory is treated as data not instructions; the store is human-inspectable/editable/deletable.

rules.text: Use native layers first, then adopt maintained tooling, build custom last. Ladder: CLAUDE.md/MEMORY.md → Skills → Hooks → API memory tool/context editing/caching → an installable MCP memory server/plugin. Write custom only for the POLICIES native tools don't provide (salience, secret-scrub, provenance, dedupe, owner-of-re-hydration).

predicate.spec: the design adopts native + maintained tooling for plumbing and confines custom code to policies (salience/scrub/provenance/dedupe/owner).

rules.text: Treat evals as the spec — write them BEFORE the agent, make memory a first-class test target: capability eval, memory assertions (write→recall; a secret must NOT persist; a planted poisoned memory must NOT change the tool call; per-user isolation), and a compaction test (after auto-compaction the agent still states the correct next action / obeys the load-bearing constraint). Graduate passing tests into a ~100%-pass regression suite gating every code change AND every model swap.

predicate.spec: acceptance evals exist before/with the agent, including the four memory tests + a compaction-retention test; a regression suite gates changes and model swaps.

rules.text: In production the memory store is an operational AND security surface — observe it (OTel-GenAI + custom growth/hit-rate/staleness metrics), guard it at the retrieval rail (memory poisoning is a named OWASP threat; retrieved memory = data), scrub secrets at write, version the agent contract AND memory schema with semver, re-eval on model deprecation, keep a GDPR-Art-17 hard-delete path (vectors included).

predicate.spec: observability + retrieval-rail guard + write-time scrub + semver'd contract/schema + model-swap re-eval + hard-delete path are present for a production agent.

rules.text: Writing to PROCEDURAL memory (rules/skills) is significantly riskier than writing to episodic/semantic (CoALA) — it can introduce bugs or subvert designer intent. Update rules/skills far more cautiously than facts.
Dedup against existing memory before writing — retrieve near-duplicates and UPDATE rather than append (mem0 ADD/UPDATE/DELETE/NOOP; ExpeL ADD/UPVOTE/DOWNVOTE/EDIT for rules).

predicate.spec: writes retrieve neighbors and update/merge rather than blindly append; a supersession mechanism exists.

rules.text: A learning agent needs BOTH write-time reflection (turn experience into a candidate memory) and read-time retrieval (surface the right memory). Log-only never generalizes; retrieve-only drowns in raw episodes. The loop: act → reflect → salience-gate → dedup/merge → periodically consolidate episodes into semantics → retrieve precisely.

Keep a small VERBATIM do-not-lose block outside the lossy summary, and an explicit NEXT ACTION line, in the handover. Gate handover delete on successful re-hydration; rotate (timestamped) rather than hard-delete to avoid a mistimed read destroying the bridge.

predicate.spec: handover has an explicit next-action line + a verbatim do-not-lose block; delete is gated on re-hydration or the handover is rotated not deleted.

rules.text: Trigger the persist proactively at ~70–80% of the context window (MemGPT memory-pressure headroom), via CLAUDE_AUTOCOMPACT_PCT_OVERRIDE, so there is room left to write the handover; combine token-threshold, turn-count, tool-output watermark, and model self-signal, acting on whichever trips first.

predicate.spec: proactive compaction threshold set (~70–80%); persist runs before the window is exhausted.

rules.text: Rank retrieval by recency × importance × relevance (importance is a write-time 1–10 signal; recency+relevance at read time). Surface each memory's age; re-verify volatile old facts rather than trust; prefer temporal invalidation (mark invalid-from) over deletion; apply principled forgetting (access reinforces, disuse expires).

predicate.spec: retrieval combines recency+importance+relevance; volatile facts are age-surfaced and re-verified; forgetting/invalidation policy exists.

rules.text: Reload the expensive, non-derivable facts; RE-DERIVE the cheap, volatile ones fresh (a reloaded volatile fact is a stale fact). Deciding which is which is the core skill.
rules.reviewer_criterion: Does the design correctly reload durable/expensive facts and re-derive volatile/cheap state rather than trusting stale reloads?

rules.text: One owner per responsibility: never run two systems that both inject at SessionStart or both auto-capture (they fight, duplicate context, double token cost). Verify every third-party tool before install (name-hallucination is the #1 hazard); check license (AGPL/Elastic/Unlicensed watch-outs); prefer self-hosted/no-phone-home for private work; enable heavyweight tooling per-project not globally.

predicate.spec: exactly one owner each for store/re-hydration/capture; adopted tools are verified + license-checked + scoped per-project.

rules.text: Borrow mem0's ADD/UPDATE/DELETE/NOOP loop, Zep/Graphiti bi-temporal invalidate-don't-delete, LangMem's type taxonomy + procedural-via-prompt-optimization, Letta's editable in-context blocks, and hot-path-vs-background consolidation. Avoid: self-reported LOCOMO/DMR rankings as a deciding factor, naive per-turn hot-path consolidation, mutate-in-place when you need history, last-write-wins shared state without serialized writes, assuming the OpenAI API gives you memory, opaque non-inspectable stores, and graph-heavy stacks for simple preference memory (start files→vector→graph as scale demands).
Auditability & user control are first-class: the user must be able to inspect, edit, and delete any memory. Favor a human-readable file-first durable layer even when a vector store backs it.

predicate.spec: a human-readable/editable/deletable durable layer exists (files), not only opaque vector blobs.

rules.text: Choose a WORKFLOW (predefined code paths) for predictability; an AGENT (LLM directs its own process) only when the path can't be pre-defined. Find the simplest solution possible; add complexity only when it demonstrably improves outcomes. Give the autonomous loop ground-truth feedback each step, human checkpoints, and stopping conditions (max iterations).
rules.reviewer_criterion: Is this the simplest architecture that meets the goal (workflow vs agent chosen correctly), with stopping conditions and human checkpoints where warranted?

rules.text: Design a FEW thoughtful tools, not API wrappers: namespace related tools; return high-signal context (resolve UUIDs to meaningful names, offer concise/detailed format); token-efficient with pagination/truncation and a sane default cap (~25k); actionable errors; prompt-engineer the descriptions and treat tool specs as versioned, evaluated assets.

predicate.spec: the built agent's tools are few, namespaced, high-signal, token-bounded, with actionable errors and versioned descriptions.

rules.text: An agent = Model + Tools + Instructions (with guardrails). Start SINGLE-agent (one model + tools + instructions in a loop); go multi-agent only when complexity warrants — manager pattern (agents-as-tools) or decentralized handoff. Layer guardrails (relevance, safety, PII, moderation, tool safeguards, rules-based, output validation, human-in-the-loop for high-risk/low-confidence).

predicate.spec: single-agent-first is honored (multi-agent only justified by complexity); layered guardrails present for a risk-bearing agent.

rules.text: Meet the safety standards for a memory-holding agent: least privilege (minimum tool scopes, read-only where possible), human-in-the-loop for high-risk actions, sandboxing/bounded autonomy (stopping conditions, rate limits, session isolation), defense-in-depth (layered guardrails). Validate documents before ingest into the memory/RAG base; screen memory at the retrieval rail; map controls to OWASP LLM Top-10 (2025) + NIST AI 600-1.

predicate.spec: least-privilege tools + HITL for high-risk + bounded autonomy + retrieval-rail validation are present; controls map to OWASP/NIST.

rules.text: If you build an LLM-as-judge: use a low-cardinality (binary + reason) reference-guided rubric; guard position bias by grading BOTH orderings (declare a winner only if consistent, else tie/escalate); test verbosity bias; use a DIFFERENT model family (self-enhancement bias) or ensemble; calibrate judge↔human agreement (Cohen's κ) before trusting it as a gate and re-measure whenever the judge model changes.

predicate.spec: any LLM-judge is binary+reference-guided, position-swap-consistent, cross-family/ensembled, and calibrated against human labels before gating.

rules.text: Red-team the memory/context: plant a poisoned 'fact' and assert it does not change the tool call; write instruction-bearing text to memory and assert it is not obeyed; establish a load-bearing constraint, force compaction, and assert it survives. Screen RAG/memory chunks at a retrieval rail before they enter the prompt.

predicate.spec: memory-poisoning, injection-into-store, and compaction-survival red-team tests exist and pass; a retrieval rail screens memory chunks.

rules.text: TDD for agents (evals-first): write executable acceptance evals FIRST; build an isolated, deterministically-seeded harness (fresh store per trial — no shared state); pick graders (deterministic → LLM → human), grade final state not rigid tool order; run red on purpose; implement to green; graduate to a ~100%-pass CI regression suite run on every change and model swap; calibrate any judge before trusting it.

predicate.spec: acceptance evals precede implementation; trials are isolated/seeded; grading is on final state; a CI regression suite gates changes+model swaps.

rules.text: Measure with STATE-BASED success as the headline and pass^k (reliability, all-k-succeed) not just pass@k; report cost + latency p50/p95 as a Pareto frontier. Report a clustered standard error under every score, compare versions with a paired/clustered difference (not overlapping error bars), and gate CI on the lower CI bound, not the point estimate.

predicate.spec: reported metrics include state-based success + pass^k + cost + p95 with clustered SEs; CI gates on the lower bound.

rules.text: Treat the agent as a versioned system with a mutable store: semver the contract (system prompt + tool schemas + config + memory schema) and version the memory schema INDEPENDENTLY; monitor drift (incl. embedding-space); on any model upgrade/deprecation re-run evals + diff behavior (tool-call format, abstention, trajectory, pass^k) and pin model snapshots; re-embed the whole corpus on an embedding-model change; keep GDPR-Art-17 hard-delete (vectors + derived nodes) + retention/TTL + audit logs.

predicate.spec: semver'd contract + independently-versioned memory schema + drift monitors + model-swap re-eval + re-embed plan + hard-delete/audit are in place.

rules.text: Production reliability: retries with jittered exponential backoff + a retry budget at ONE layer; circuit breakers; idempotency keys on every MUTATING tool; graceful degradation of the memory layer (fall back to no-memory/cached rather than fail the turn); human-in-the-loop gates + max-iterations; schema-validate-then-repair on tool output.

predicate.spec: backoff+jitter+retry-budget, circuit breakers, idempotency keys on mutating tools, memory graceful-degradation, HITL+max-iters, and validate-then-repair are present for a production agent.

rules.text: Cost discipline: front-load a stable cache prefix (system + tools + long-lived memory index) so re-hydration is a cheap cache read; use model tiering/effort over switching models; spend the always-loaded budget on the smallest high-signal set at the right altitude, with examples over exhaustive rules, positive framing, and concrete+motivated instructions.

predicate.spec: stable prefix is cache-front-loaded; always-loaded context is minimal/high-signal with examples and positive framing.

rules.text: THE core principle (and the reason Genesis's hooks exist): expertise usage is NEVER made deterministic by putting it in context — CLAUDE.md/auto-memory are 'context, not enforced configuration'. Determinism is a property of the harness ACTION (a hook), not the model's cognition. Injection guarantees delivery, never obedience; determinism is recovered only by a VALIDATOR closing the loop on a checkable predicate. Judgment (non-checkable) properties relocate determinism to a second model, they do not recover it.

Realize deterministic expertise as an INJECT → GATE → VALIDATE hook triple over a DECOUPLED, versioned store (skill / knowledge file / MCP server / subagent prompt): INJECT the relevant expertise at the right altitude (SessionStart always-on; UserPromptSubmit/PreToolUse action-specific); GATE risky actions on observable preconditions (PreToolUse deny/exit 2); VALIDATE checkable rules and refuse to finish until they pass (PostToolUse correct; Stop/SubagentStop force rework). Enforce capability boundaries at the TOOL layer.

predicate.spec: the built agent has a decoupled expertise store + inject/gate/validate hooks wired; checkable rules are enforced by gate/validate; boundaries enforced by the tool list.

rules.text: For SEMANTIC quality that no regex can check, add an evaluator subagent or prompt hook — and accept this layer is probabilistic; make it a majority-vote / panel if stakes justify. Do not treat a probabilistic pass as proof.
rules.reviewer_criterion: Is the semantic-quality layer an independent evaluator (panel if high-stakes), treated as advisory-not-proof, not the author self-grading?

rules.text: Hook-wiring correctness: only SessionStart / UserPromptSubmit / UserPromptExpansion inject RAW stdout as context — every other event must emit the additionalContext JSON field. Write injected context as factual statements (not out-of-band commands) or prompt-injection defenses surface it; cap output at 10,000 chars. PreToolUse decisions go in hookSpecificOutput (allow/deny/ask/defer; deny>defer>ask>allow); a PreToolUse hook cannot compel a tool the model never calls and @-referenced files bypass it; PostToolUse is corrective (cannot undo side effects). Pick one channel (exit code OR exit-0 JSON), never both.

predicate.spec: hooks use additionalContext JSON where stdout isn't injected, factual framing, <=10k chars, correct decision fields, single channel; injected content isn't out-of-band commands.

rules.text: Everything is INFERENCE-TIME: fine-tuning (the only intrinsic 'always') is out of scope — not available under Max, and the least decoupled. Learning happens through memory and context, never weight updates. Genesis runs inference-time only.

2026 capability deltas to exploit/respect: subagent RESUMABILITY (SendMessage/TaskStop auto-resume; a user-stopped subagent does not), Agent TEAMS (experimental, env-flagged), ~30 hook events (wider inject/gate/validate attachment surface), memory tool GA, context editing + server-side compaction, new subagent frontmatter (memory/isolation/effort/hooks/mcpServers — plugin subagents silently ignore hooks/mcpServers/permissionMode), a per-session subagent-spawn cap (default 200 — log what's dropped), output styles (behavior not knowledge/enforcement), plugins as the distribution unit, subagent output scanning (shallow marker, defense-in-depth).
